# MESA — Memory Engine for Structured Agents

[![MESA CI](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Yasou13/MESA)](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/releases/latest)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Yasou13/MESA)](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![Python: 3.11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11%2B-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/pyproject.toml)

MESA is an LLM-independent, source-linked memory engine for AI applications. It stores documents with exact provenance (document, revision, passage) and returns verifiable, scoped evidence over HTTP, Python SDK, and MCP. MESA returns evidence; it never writes the final answer or hallucinates sources.

Package version: **0.9.0**. V4 is the current API. Production qualification remains at the release candidate stage: **NO-GO** until the [release gates](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/docs/release.md) pass.

## Installation

```bash
pip install "mesa-memory[adapters]"
```

Supported on Linux and macOS natively. On Windows, run via Docker or WSL.

## Start the server

```bash
mesa start
```

Starts the local server on `http://127.0.0.1:8000`, initializes storage at `~/.mesa/data`, and creates credentials at `~/.mesa/credentials.json` (mode 0600).

## Add and search documents

In another terminal, add and search documents immediately:

```bash
mesa add document.txt --source file://document.txt
mesa search "your query"
```

## Python SDK

```python
from mesa_client import Mesa

mesa = Mesa()
mesa.add(open("document.txt").read(), source="file://document.txt")
print(mesa.context("your query"))
```

`Mesa()` uses `MESA_API_KEY` and `MESA_BASE_URL` when they are set, otherwise the local credentials in `~/.mesa/credentials.json`.

## Connect MCP clients

Generate a ready-to-paste configuration block for Claude Desktop or any MCP client:

```bash
mesa mcp-config
```

## Internal models (optional)

Models stay off by default. Documents are stored and found through BM25 lexical search without any model running. `FactExtractionService` owns canonical V4 extraction when models are enabled.

To enable semantic vector search and fact extraction with local Ollama, add to `~/.mesa/.env`:

```bash
MESA_MODEL_ENABLED=true
MESA_LLM_MODEL=ollama:qwen2.5:7b
MESA_EMBEDDING_MODEL=ollama:bge-m3
```

Local `openai_compatible` servers (such as vLLM started with `--port 8001`, at `MESA_LLM_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`; MESA itself uses port 8000) are also allowed with `MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` on a local endpoint (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `host.docker.internal`) and require no API key (D31). For cloud model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic), set `MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=true` and provide the required API keys.

## Graph toggle

To run without the Kùzu graph database, set:

```bash
MESA_GRAPH_ENABLED=false
```

GRAPH lanes end `SKIPPED`, and turning the flag back on later backfills the graph at startup.

## Docker

Run MESA in a single-user local container (D32):

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml up --build -d
```

Credentials are written to `/var/lib/mesa/credentials.json` in the container volume:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml exec mesa-v4 cat /var/lib/mesa/credentials.json
docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml exec -T mesa-v4 mesa add - --source file://document.txt < document.txt
docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml exec mesa-v4 mesa search "your query"
```

No variables are required; models and external providers default off. If you set `MESA_API_KEY` and `MESA_PRINCIPAL_ID` for existing HTTP clients, the server accepts that key too, and the `mesa` commands inside the container use it first; add `-e MESA_API_KEY=` after `exec` to use the local credentials instead. The image includes `adapters`; build with `--build-arg MESA_EXTRAS=ml,adapters` to add local sentence-transformers. Ollama defaults to `http://host.docker.internal:11434` (the Docker host).

## Google Colab

Run MESA with GPU-accelerated Ollama in Colab:
[Colab Quickstart](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/examples/colab_quickstart.ipynb)

## Development

```bash
uv sync --locked --python 3.11
```

See [testing](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/docs/testing.md) for local tests, and [docs/testing.md](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/docs/testing.md) for test markers.

## Documentation

- [Getting Started Guide](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)
- [Configuration Reference](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/docs/configuration.md)
- [API Reference](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/docs/api-reference.md)
- [MCP Integration Guide](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/README_MCP.md)
- [Architecture](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Documentation Index](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/main/docs/README.md)

pages.raw_markdown: # Installation and first run This guide covers getting started with MESA as a new user, from installation to querying evidence, followed by advanced operator provisioning and production runtime profiles. Production qualification remains at the release candidate stage: **NO-GO** until the [release gates](docs/core/release-policy/) pass for the intended commit. ## Installation Install MESA with the adapters extra: ```bash pip install "mesa-memory[adapters]" ``` Supported natively on Linux and macOS. On Windows, use Docker or WSL. The development version can be installed directly from git: `pip install "mesa-memory[adapters] @ git+https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA"`. Or install from source with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/): ```bash git clone https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA.git cd MESA uv sync --locked --python 3.11 uv pip check ``` ## Quickstart ### 1. Start the server For standard local usage, `mesa start` automatically provisions local storage (`~/.mesa/data`), writes credentials (`~/.mesa/credentials.json`), sets model-disabled defaults, and starts the loopback server on `http://127.0.0.1:8000`: ```bash mesa start ``` ### 2. Add and search documents In another terminal, add and search documents immediately without manual credential configuration: ```bash mesa add document.txt --source file://document.txt mesa search "your query" mesa status ``` ### 3. Python SDK Use the high-level `Mesa` client to ingest documents and query evidence contexts: ```python from mesa_client import Mesa mesa = Mesa() mesa.add(open("document.txt").read(), source="file://document.txt") print(mesa.context("your query")) ``` `Mesa()` uses `MESA_API_KEY` and `MESA_BASE_URL` when they are set, otherwise the local credentials in `~/.mesa/credentials.json`. ### 4. Connect MCP clients Connect Claude Desktop or any MCP client by generating a ready-to-paste configuration block: ```bash mesa mcp-config ``` ### 5. Internal models (optional) Models stay off by default. Documents are stored and found through BM25 lexical search without any model running. To enable semantic vector search and fact extraction with local Ollama, add to `~/.mesa/.env`: ```bash MESA_MODEL_ENABLED=true MESA_LLM_MODEL=ollama:qwen2.5:7b MESA_EMBEDDING_MODEL=ollama:bge-m3 ``` Under decision D31, local `openai_compatible` servers (e.g. vLLM started with `--port 8001`, at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`, since MESA itself uses port 8000) are also permitted with `MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` on a local endpoint and require no API key. For external cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic), set `MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=true` and supply the required API keys. Missing extras raise clear, actionable installation messages: - Ollama LLM, Ollama embedding, or OpenAI-compatible embedding → `pip install "mesa-memory[adapters]"` - Local embedding (`sentence-transformers`) → `pip install "mesa-memory[ml]"` ### 6. Graph toggle To run without the Kùzu graph database, set: ```bash MESA_GRAPH_ENABLED=false ``` GRAPH lanes end `SKIPPED`, and turning the flag back on later backfills the graph at startup. ### 7. Docker Run MESA in a single-user local container (D32): ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml up --build -d ``` Credentials are written to `/var/lib/mesa/credentials.json` in the container volume: ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml exec mesa-v4 cat /var/lib/mesa/credentials.json docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml exec -T mesa-v4 mesa add - --source file://document.txt < document.txt docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml exec mesa-v4 mesa search "your query" ``` No environment variables are required: models and external providers default off. The image runs `mesa start --host 0.0.0.0` as a non-root user; Compose publishes only `127.0.0.1:8000`. Credentials retain a loopback base URL for CLI use inside the container. The named volume keeps data and credentials on restart. `MESA_API_KEY` and `MESA_PRINCIPAL_ID` are optional for existing bootstrap setups; when set, the `mesa` commands inside the container use that key first, so add `-e MESA_API_KEY=` after `exec` to use the local credentials. Ollama defaults to `http://host.docker.internal:11434`, which reaches the Docker host. The default image includes `adapters`; add sentence-transformers with `docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml build --build-arg MESA_EXTRAS=ml,adapters`. ### 8. Google Colab Run MESA with GPU-accelerated Ollama in Google Colab: [Colab Quickstart](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/examples/colab_quickstart.ipynb) ## Using MESA with your LLM When connecting an external language model to answer questions from MESA memory, supply a system prompt that enforces untrusted data boundaries and precise source citations. `mesa_client` exports `RECOMMENDED_SYSTEM_PROMPT` for this purpose: ```python from mesa_client import AsyncMesaV4Client, RECOMMENDED_SYSTEM_PROMPT # System prompt for answering LLMs: system_prompt = RECOMMENDED_SYSTEM_PROMPT # Retrieved memory context goes into the prompt/message: async with AsyncMesaV4Client(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000", api_key=api_key) as client: bundle = await client.get_context(session_id=session_id, query="What is the policy?") user_message = f"{bundle['context']}\n\nQuestion: What is the policy?" ``` The context returned in `bundle["context"]` is deterministically wrapped in `...`. The prompt instructs the model to treat everything within those tags strictly as data, never follow instructions contained within them, cite document and revision IDs for every claim, and decline to answer if the evidence is insufficient. --- ## Advanced Operator & Production Profiles Use Python 3.11–3.13 (the CI matrix) and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). Docker with Compose is needed only for containers. Run from the repository: ```bash uv sync --locked --python 3.11 uv pip check ``` [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/pyproject.toml) declares supported dependency ranges and [uv.lock](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/uv.lock) fixes the graph used by CI/Docker. CI pins its installer version in the workflow; an installed dependency range is not a model download. Choose `--python 3.11`, `3.12` or `3.13` if appropriate. Leaving the interpreter unspecified can select a newer Python outside the tested matrix. Use `uv sync --locked --python 3.11 --extra dev` when running developer tests. SQLite (with FTS5) comes from the Python interpreter; LanceDB, PyArrow and Kùzu are installed as core Python dependencies. No separate database server, Docker container, manual SQL import or ML extra is needed for models-disabled startup. Native wheels depend on Python/platform availability. The isolated installation verified for this guide is Linux x86_64 / Python 3.11; other platforms were not verified in this developer-experience pass. | Extra | When needed | |---|---| | `dev` | Local checks and development | | `adapters` | Provider SDK integrations | | `ml` | Local transformer/embedding dependencies | | `loadtest` | Explicit load-test work | | `mcp` | Compatibility extra; MCP itself is already a core dependency | For a provider setup that needs both SDKs and local models: ```bash uv sync --locked --python 3.11 --extra adapters --extra ml uv pip check ``` Install only the extras needed by the selected runtime. Model downloads, credentials and operational provider endpoints are separate prerequisites. ### Choose topology and storage | Use | Profile / Compose file | Storage rule | |---|---|---| | Canonical V4 | `combined` / `docker-compose.v4.yml` | One process owns API, consumers and stores | | Local model-disabled startup | `combined`, models/providers false | V4 storage and BM25 search without model calls | Choose a dedicated absolute writable storage root. Do not use the repository, home directory or filesystem root. V3 and V4 must not write the same root. Fresh combined startup initializes the databases automatically; keep SQLite, LanceDB, Kùzu and the policy database together under that root. The runtime has one owner: stop it before running offline admin or migration commands. The runtime does not load `.env` implicitly; the explicit dotenv precedence is explained in [configuration](docs/core/configuration/). ### Native V4 startup Before startup: 1. Select a new or compatible V4 storage root and provision credentials/ACL using [runbook section 2](docs/core/operations/#credential-bootstrap). 2. Install the selected extraction and embedding dependencies; configure their provider/model identity. External `text-embedding-3-small` requires dimension 1536; the local Magibu default is 768. Equal dimensions alone are insufficient. 3. Select validation mode. Mode 0 has no LLM validator but still needs canonical extraction and embeddings; mode 2 requires distinct A/B validator identities. 4. Supply the issued API key and provider secrets privately to the process. Example profile after those prerequisites (the storage path is an operator example, not an automatically provisioned directory): ```bash export MESA_STORAGE_ROOT=/srv/mesa/v4-data export MESA_RUNTIME_PROFILE=combined export MESA_LOAD_DOTENV=false export MESA_MODEL_ENABLED=true export MESA_TIER3_MODE=0 export MESA_PRINCIPAL_ID=service-api # Set MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED to match the reviewed providers. .venv/bin/python -m mesa_memory.runtime_entrypoint ``` The launcher binds `0.0.0.0`; use the explicit loopback command from the quickstart for local use. Readiness is `/health/init`; `/health` requires a key. The [V4 example](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/examples/v4_quickstart.py) creates the catalog and session, inserts a source, polls its mutation and checks evidence. Its `docs-*` identities require the grants shown in the quickstart. ### Compose V4 provisions local credentials automatically, with models and external providers off. Existing deployments may supply `MESA_API_KEY` and `MESA_PRINCIPAL_ID` privately. For model-enabled operation, set the model flags and provider configuration above: ```bash docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml config --quiet docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml up --build -d docker compose -f docker-compose.v4.yml ps ``` For V3 lexical compatibility: ```bash docker compose config --quiet docker compose up --build -d ``` Compose publishes the API on loopback. V4 mounts its named volume under `/var/lib/mesa`, with storage at `/var/lib/mesa/data`. Host provisioning against `/srv/mesa/v4-data` does not provision that named volume: run admin commands against the actual deployment's policy database, with the same credential and ACL scope. Do not add a second writer to the volume. Rendering Compose with models disabled supports V4 storage and BM25 search. ### Upgrade and verification Use [migration](docs/core/operations/#upgrade-v080) for schema/representation upgrades, [backup and restore](docs/core/operations/#6-backup-restore-ve-v4-rebuild) for recovery, and [projection rebuild](docs/core/rebuild-runbook/) for the offline runner. Projection rebuild does not convert a V3 database to V4. Run [developer checks](docs/core/testing/) for the affected contracts. Passing these checks does not replace real-provider, migration/restore or soak release evidence. ## Local quickstart Run from the repository after `uv sync --locked --python 3.11`. This uses one combined process, no model loading and no external provider access. It checks installation, credentials and readiness. This profile stores V4 records and finds them through BM25 without embedding or extraction calls. VECTOR lanes end `SKIPPED`; enable embedding later to backfill vectors at startup with the same identity. ### Automatic local bootstrap (`mesa start`) For standard local usage, `mesa start` provisions local storage (`~/.mesa/data`), initializes credentials (`~/.mesa/credentials.json`), sets model-disabled defaults, and starts the loopback server: ```bash mesa start ``` In another terminal, add and search documents immediately without manually exporting credentials: ```bash mesa add notes.txt --source file://notes.txt mesa search "notes" mesa status ``` ### Provision before startup (manual) Choose a disposable location on a disk with sufficient free space. The example uses a unique child under `~/mesa-doc-demos`; do not reuse user storage. `/tmp` may be memory-backed on some hosts. ```bash mkdir -p "$HOME/mesa-doc-demos" export MESA_STORAGE_ROOT="$(mktemp -d "$HOME/mesa-doc-demos/run-XXXXXX")" export MESA_RUNTIME_PROFILE=combined export MESA_LOAD_DOTENV=false export MESA_MODEL_ENABLED=false export MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false export MESA_TIER3_MODE=0 export MESA_PRINCIPAL_ID=docs-principal export MESA_PORT=18080 export MESA_API_KEY="$(.venv/bin/mesa-v4-admin issue-key --principal docs-principal)" .venv/bin/mesa-v4-admin grant-role --principal docs-principal --tenant docs-tenant --role OWNER .venv/bin/mesa-v4-admin grant-agent --principal docs-principal --agent docs-agent --permission SESSION_CREATE ``` Keep the issued key out of logs and shared terminal output. The commands write only the new sample policy database. Start the following server in this terminal after provisioning. For client commands, use another terminal with the same exported settings and key supplied privately; a newly opened terminal does not automatically inherit these exports: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn mesa_memory.api.server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 ``` Wait for readiness: ```bash curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:18080/health/init curl --fail -H "X-API-Key: $MESA_API_KEY" http://127.0.0.1:18080/health ``` Readiness returns `{"status":"ready"}` on success; health reports store/queue state. The normal launcher binds all interfaces internally; this explicit uvicorn command limits the local example to loopback. With `MESA_API_KEY` already exported, the same checks are available through: ```bash MESA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080 make health ``` This checks `/health/init` and authenticated `/health` with a five-second timeout per request. It exits nonzero for missing/invalid credentials, connection errors, invalid responses or unhealthy status. It does not open local databases, print credentials or follow redirects. The default base URL is `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. ### V4 canonical example (provider prerequisites) `examples/v4_quickstart.py` supplies required title/source/catalog IDs, freezes one chunk, polls the mutation and checks source-linked evidence. It works with the model-disabled combined environment above through BM25. For vector search and fact extraction, set `MESA_MODEL_ENABLED=true` (or enable each model flag separately), install the needed `ml`/`adapters` extras and provision reviewed provider/model/dimension settings. Retain the same ACL and one-owner rules. A concrete provider environment is in [minimal V4 provider setup](docs/core/configuration/#minimal-v4-provider-setup). Follow [configuration](docs/core/configuration/) and [installation](docs/core/getting-started/#installation). The exact command after those prerequisites is: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m examples.v4_quickstart ``` The example prints assertion IDs and source/dataset/chunk references after checking `COMMITTED` and provenance, then ends the session. The client's `with` block closes HTTP resources; ending a session is a separate server operation. `wait_until_committed()` can return failed terminal states; always check `state == "COMMITTED"`. A timeout does not cancel the mutation: inspect `client.status(mutation_id)` before deciding what to retry. Developer-experience verification on Linux/Python 3.11 used an isolated, non-editable locked Core install, models-disabled startup/health checks, and this V4 example with explicitly injected deterministic extraction/embedding. SQLite, LanceDB, Kùzu and background processing were real. The test limited Kùzu to a 64 MiB buffer pool, 256 MiB mapping and one query thread to fit the host's available RAM; this is test sizing, not a production capacity result. No real model was called. Real-provider V4 and Docker were **not verified** in this pass. ### Restart and cleanup Stop this example's server with Ctrl-C and restart it with the same environment. Query the saved session/mutation while the session is active. Do not run two writers. End the session only after retrieval. Reads after end depend on retained permissions; new writes require an active session. `end_session` can return `status=pending` with a `finalization_id`: finalization is durable background work, not an HTTP client close operation. After stopping the server, retain or remove only this newly created sample root using your file manager. No generic database/volume removal command is provided. If the port is occupied choose another loopback port and set `MESA_BASE_URL` for the example accordingly. ## Python SDK For local scripting, rapid prototyping, and agent applications, the high-level `Mesa` client provides a clean interface with automatic credential discovery and catalog session handling: ```python from mesa_client import Mesa mesa = Mesa() mesa.add(open("kira.txt").read(), source="file://kira.txt") print(mesa.context("kira ne zaman ödenir?")) ``` `Mesa()` automatically discovers connection settings and API keys from environment variables (`MESA_BASE_URL`, `MESA_API_KEY`) or from `/credentials.json` provisioned by `mesa start`. On first use, it ensures the configured workspace and dataset exist, starts a session, and reuses it for subsequent additions, searches, and context retrieval. ## Using MESA with your LLM When connecting an external language model to answer questions from MESA memory, supply a system prompt that enforces untrusted data boundaries and precise source citations. `mesa_client` exports `RECOMMENDED_SYSTEM_PROMPT` for this purpose: ```python from mesa_client import AsyncMesaV4Client, RECOMMENDED_SYSTEM_PROMPT # System prompt for answering LLMs: system_prompt = RECOMMENDED_SYSTEM_PROMPT # Retrieved memory context goes into the prompt/message: async with AsyncMesaV4Client(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000", api_key=api_key) as client: bundle = await client.get_context(session_id=session_id, query="What is the policy?") user_message = f"{bundle['context']}\n\nQuestion: What is the policy?" ``` The context returned in `bundle["context"]` is deterministically wrapped in `...`. # MESA Core current V4 architecture > **Package version:** 0.9.0 (unreleased; publishing is an owner step), without production certification. This document owns the current V4 design; production qualification remains release candidate / `NO-GO` under the [release policy](docs/core/release-policy/). The root [architecture entry point](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/ARCHITECTURE.md) links here. The obsolete V3 whitepaper is available in Git history; see the [ADR index](docs/core/decisions/) for decision applicability. ## Module ownership | Module | Responsibility | |---|---| | `mesa_storage` | Canonical SQLite, catalog repositories, ownership, retrieval and projection providers | | `mesa_memory` | Runtime configuration, extraction/validation, embedding, context, security and rebuild orchestration | | `mesa_workers` | Durable ingestion, projection and maintenance consumers | | `mesa_api` | HTTP schemas, authorized V3/V4 routes and control API | | `mesa_client` | Sync/async HTTP clients and optional integrations | | `mesa_mcp` | MCP service adapters, gateway, bindings and client lifecycle | | `mesa_evals` | Local repository diagnostics and deterministic retrieval contract tooling (not packaged in wheel) | Higher layers may depend on lower layers: API/MCP → workers → memory → storage. Runtime composition roots are explicit exceptions; the source guard is [`check_layer_imports.py`](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/scripts/check_layer_imports.py). `MemoryDAO` remains the compatibility façade; catalog transactions have a focused repository boundary. See ADRs [0012](docs/core/adr-0012/) and [0013](docs/core/adr-0013/). ## Runtime boundary V4 has one supported storage-writing topology: one `combined` process owns SQLite, LanceDB and Kùzu. API admission and background consumers run in that process. A second writer must never mount the same storage root. V3 remains available as the lexical-core compatibility surface and keeps its existing API/worker topology. V3 and v4 must not write the same physical storage directories concurrently. Canonical v4 fact extraction is owned by `FactExtractionService`. ## Security and catalog hierarchy The v4 security boundary is a tenant, not an agent: ```text Principal └── Tenant └── Workspace └── Dataset └── Document └── immutable DocumentRevision └── SourceChunk ``` Roles are `OWNER`, `WRITER` and `READER` at tenant, workspace or dataset scope. Roles inherit downward. Purge and rollback require explicit dataset permissions. Agent IDs represent compute/persona context and do not grant tenant access. An authenticated session is generated by the server and binds one principal, tenant, workspace, agent and immutable set of datasets. Insert, search, context, status, replay and rollback derive their scope from this record. API credentials use `key_id.secret`. Only the salted scrypt digest is stored; plaintext is returned once by `mesa-v4-admin issue-key`. Multiple keys may belong to one or more principals and can be revoked or rotated independently. ## Canonical ingestion `POST /v4/memory/insert` durably admits exact source content and creates: - one `MemoryCandidate`; - one `memory_mutations` ledger row; - one `pipeline_runs` row plus append-only events; - ordered SQL, vector and graph outbox lanes. The candidate explicitly carries tenant, workspace, dataset, document, revision, chunk, source reference, evidence span, agent/session, pipeline, extraction and embedding versions. Authorization fields are never read from free-form metadata. An authenticated dataset writer may additionally supply the typed `legal_identity` object (required `law_id` and `article_id`; optional `statute_code` and version/paragraph/clause identifiers). MESA validates it against the bounded legal alias ontology, binds it to the immutable mutation provenance and stores it on canonical assertions. Reserved `_mesa_*` keys in caller metadata are always discarded, so free-form metadata cannot opt into legal ranking. The producer remains responsible for verifying that the declared identity belongs to the source; MESA_Data must not populate it from a bare article heading. Validation is an explicit policy gate configured via `MESA_TIER3_MODE` (0 = deterministic-only, 1 = single LLM validator, 2 = dual-LLM consensus). A rejected mutation may keep its raw audit source, but it cannot create an active SQL, vector, entity, edge or assertion artifact. In Mode 0, deterministic admission checks gate progression with zero LLM validator dependencies. ## Pipeline and failure model The legal success path is: ```text QUEUED → RUNNING → EXTRACTED → VALIDATED → PROJECTING → COMMITTED ``` Failure/recovery states are `RETRY_PENDING`, `DLQ`, `ROLLING_BACK`, `ROLLED_BACK` and `BLOCKED`. State changes use compare-and-swap and append an event. Claims use a random fencing token, bounded lease, heartbeat and bounded retry. A worker that loses its token cannot finalize the claim. V4 retries restart extraction from `RETRY_PENDING`, skip model calls after validation, and atomically mark the dispatch and any not-yet-validated mutation `DEAD_LETTER` and the raw log `failed` after five unsuccessful attempts, preserving final states. Failed dispatch and projection attempts back off for 60, 120, 240 and 480 seconds, capped at 900 seconds, before becoming eligible for another claim. At startup, the combined runtime holds the storage writer lock and returns abandoned processing raw logs to `DEFERRED`, clearing their claims. Operator replay also resets an extraction dead letter's dispatch attempts and raw-log claim, making it eligible to run immediately. These are pipeline states; client-facing mutation states are listed in [concepts and ingestion](docs/core/concepts-and-ingestion/). `COMMITTED` is the success state; receiving an admission response alone does not establish completion. Projection prerequisites are enforced in the database: ```text SQL → vector → graph ``` The projector only claims a later lane when its predecessor is complete. Every lane is idempotent by mutation and physical artifact identity. Legal citation retrieval selects trusted typed identities through the scoped compound assertion index before lane ranking. Tenant, dataset, agent, jurisdiction, validity and committed-state predicates are applied in that SQL selection. Typed identity refines candidate recall and lane order; it does not bypass deterministic weighted RRF or replace canonical evidence text. ## Canonical entity and Graph V2 Entity IDs use a fixed UUID5 namespace: ```text UUID5(namespace, tenant_id + entity_type + identity_key) ``` `identity_key` is the normalized ontology URI when supplied; otherwise it is the Unicode NFKC, whitespace-normalized and case-folded canonical name. Resolution order is ontology/external ID, registered alias, canonical name, then create. Collisions produce a deterministic redirect; historical rows are retained. Canonical SQLite connections use WAL and `synchronous=FULL` by default; weaker synchronization is restricted to the explicit test profile. This does not create a transaction spanning SQLite, LanceDB and Kùzu. SQLite is authoritative for `v4_entities` and immutable `v4_assertions`. Kùzu is an idempotent projection. Assertions include subject, predicate, entity or literal object, document/revision/chunk source, evidence span, jurisdiction, authority, confidence, validity interval, mutation and pipeline run. Assertion identity includes predicate, source and temporal context, so different relations between the same entities remain distinct. `CONTRADICTS` and `SUPERSEDES` connect assertions and preserve provenance. PageRank only publishes observation telemetry; it cannot quarantine, tombstone, delete or otherwise change retrieval eligibility. ## Artifact ownership and rollback `artifact_registry` represents physical SQL, vector and graph artifacts. `artifact_sources` allows several mutations/source chunks to own the same entity or vector. Rollback removes only the requesting run's source ownership. A shared artifact remains active while another source owns it. The last-owner path writes the SQLite retrieval tombstone first and schedules idempotent vector/graph cleanup. An unfinished cleanup leaves the run `BLOCKED`, never falsely committed. A new document revision does not erase history. Prior assertions become `SUPERSEDED`. A legal purge retracts the requested source and removes only artifacts that have no remaining active owner. ## Reconciliation and health Reconciliation is bidirectional: - ledger artifact missing from a store: requeue the missing lane; - physical artifact without registry/ownership: quarantine it in the registry and enqueue cleanup. Authenticated `/health` returns the aggregate fields `status`, `maintenance` and `rebuild_state`. `/health/init` reports readiness and fails with HTTP 503 when required stores, workers or backlog checks fail. Projection backlog, dead letter, stuck leases, cleanup backlog, blocked cleanup, ownerless registry rows and shared-owner counts are aggregate gauges at `/metrics`; they are not individual fields in the public `/health` response. ## Retrieval All SQL, vector and graph lanes receive the authorized dataset filter before ranking. V4 combines rank positions using real reciprocal rank fusion. Jurisdiction and validity constrain eligibility before ranking; assertion confidence affects assertion-lane ordering. The bounded post-RRF legal factor uses query statute/article identity. See [retrieval](docs/core/retrieval-and-graph/). Candidate assertion identity is the deterministic final tie-break. Responses include document, revision, chunk, evidence, assertion, pipeline and embedding provenance. PageRank is not a retrieval eligibility signal. ### Bounded adaptive context retrieval The raw V4 search endpoint remains the deterministic single-query primitive. The context endpoint and `mesa_get_context` default to `retrieval_mode=single`. Callers may explicitly select `adaptive`, which runs the original query first and invokes one semantic reformulation call only when the result is empty or none of its top three candidates has support from at least two retrieval lanes. The planner receives only the normalized user query and may return at most two validated query strings. It cannot change tenant, agent, dataset, jurisdiction, temporal or graph scope. New statute/article citations are rejected. Every expansion reuses `MemoryDAO.search_v4_memory`; query rankings are fused with deterministic RRF weights Q0=1.0, Q1=0.5 and Q2=0.5, with a Q0-preserving tie break. Inner lane scores and provenance remain unchanged, and outer `query_origins` plus `query_fusion_score` remain separately auditable. An adaptive request performs at most one planner call and three total retrievals. Planner or optional expansion failures preserve the original retrieval. The deduplicated final candidate list enters the existing `ContextBuilder` once, so the 2048-token default and atomic proof packing remain the sole model-visible budget authority. This feature performs no answer generation, recursive planning, decomposition or reranking. ## Migration and release V3 and V4 use separate storage roots. Moving V3 content into V4 requires an explicit source/catalog mapping and ingestion through the V4 contract; there is no general automatic V3-to-V4 converter documented here. The offline projection runner rebuilds derived stores from an existing V4 canonical ledger, not a new ledger from raw V3 data. For V4 upgrades use [migration](docs/core/operations/#upgrade-v080), [backup/restore](docs/core/operations/#6-backup-restore-ve-v4-rebuild) and the [projection rebuild procedure](docs/core/rebuild-runbook/). Keep the prior root and matching code/config for rollback. Production remains `NO-GO` until migration/restore, v4 Compose, crash, saturation, cross-tenant concurrency, benchmark and 24-hour soak gates all pass with production-like storage and the selected model provider. Canonical V4 insertion requires the combined processing consumer. With models off, it stores records with a `SKIPPED` VECTOR lane and finds them through BM25. Enabling embedding later backfills skipped lanes without hiding committed records. ## Ecosystem and ownership | Project | Ownership | Core release implication | |---|---|---| | MESA Core | Runtime, catalog/mutations, projections, scoped retrieval, SDK/MCP | This repository's package and GitHub release only | | MESA_Data | Source acquisition, metadata/identity, revisions/chunking, native publisher | Producer must satisfy Core ingestion and provenance contracts | | MESA_E2E_Certification | Freeze, official TEST, sealed answer context, scorer and verdict | Independent certification; Core unit tests cannot change its verdict | | mesa_benchmark | Comparative methodology, runner, external datasets/judges | Core `mesa_evals` is historical diagnostics plus deterministic RRF contract tooling | | MESA_Law | Legal product/integration work outside Core | No Core legal-advice or legal-certification guarantee | | mesa-model-tests | Independent DEV model qualification | Model quality and pending human review are separate from Core release | The source consumer contract is [concepts and ingestion](docs/core/concepts-and-ingestion/) and [API](docs/core/api-reference/). Supply exact content, immutable revision/chunk IDs, source references and verified legal identity where appropriate. Core validates schema/alias consistency and linkage; it does not fetch official laws or establish that producer metadata is legally correct. SDK insertion currently lacks the HTTP `legal_identity` parameter; use reviewed HTTP payloads for this contract. Comparative benchmark methodology lives in the external `mesa_benchmark` project's `docs/METHODOLOGY.md`. Core retains [`tests/test_v4_rrf_ablation.py`](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/tests/test_v4_rrf_ablation.py) and [`mesa_evals/v4_rrf_ablation.py`](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/mesa_evals/v4_rrf_ablation.py) for deterministic retrieval contracts; these are not comparative model-quality measurements. Official certification is owned and executed outside Core. A Core documentation edit or unit-test result cannot change a sealed certification verdict. External repository commit IDs and measured outcomes belong in dated evidence records, not this ownership map. Core `ContextBuilder` budget/provenance behavior and Profile B's independently sealed Top-5/context/scorer settings are distinct contracts. A successful Core DEV example proves the exercised path only, not native ecosystem delivery or model accuracy. Provider pairing quality requires its own measured evidence. ## Performance and limitations No v0.8.0 throughput, recall, accuracy, latency or 10–20 GB corpus-capacity result has been measured in this documentation release. A unit/fixture smoke is not a production soak, and bounded graph traversal does not guarantee complete recall. Historical benchmark and audit documents have been retired from the working tree. Earlier reports in Git history describe their own fixtures and revisions, not current capacity or a completed 24-hour release gate. Use [release requirements](docs/core/release-policy/) to evaluate evidence for a specific commit; missing raw results or run artifacts are unavailable evidence. `VectorEngine` maintenance defaults to 128 mutations and cleans old versions older than seven days. Compaction, deduplication and executor cleanup mitigate growth; they do not establish bounded long-soak RSS for every workload. Watch fragments, version metadata, RSS, disk, mutation latency and maintenance failure counts. Retained projection generations/backups are not automatically deleted. Queue admission defaults are 50,000 pending records / 2 GiB, with tenant-aware bounds and bounded in-flight/retry capacity. They are safety limits, not tested throughput commitments. See [configuration](docs/core/configuration/). SQL writers are serialized; one combined owner is required per storage root. Advisory local locking is not a distributed/NFS coordinator. ### Compatibility evidence | Area | Source of support/configuration | Evidence needed | |---|---|---| | Python | `pyproject.toml`; CI matrix 3.11–3.13 | Successful jobs for the target commit | | OS | CI uses Ubuntu; no full OS support matrix declared | Target-platform validation | | Dependencies | Ranges in `pyproject.toml`, exact graph in `uv.lock` | Locked install and compatibility check | | Storage | SQLite FTS5, LanceDB, Kùzu | Native-store contracts plus representative capacity/recovery runs | | Models | Explicit provider/model identity | Real-provider behavior, quality and cost measurements | | Docker | Dockerfile and two Compose topologies | Image and deployment evidence for the target commit | ### Unsupported or constrained Bitemporal queries, associative PPR, human legal certification, distributed writers/hosted storage, Ladybug backend, online or tenant/dataset-scoped rebuild, automatic retained-generation cleanup and guaranteed citation correctness are not current Core guarantees. V4 retrieval performs no answer generation. Adaptive planning is opt-in, bounded and not recursive.

# Concepts and ingestion lifecycle

## Identity and scope

| Concept | Implemented meaning |
|---|---|
| Principal | Server-authenticated identity owning keys and ACL grants |
| Tenant | V4 authorization boundary |
| Workspace | Tenant-owned grouping of datasets |
| Dataset | Source collection inside a workspace; session-bound access |
| Agent | Compute/persona context; not a tenant credential |
| Session | Server-generated principal/scope binding with immutable dataset set |
| Document | Dataset-owned source identity with a current revision head |
| Revision | Immutable source version with a frozen chunk manifest |
| Source chunk | Exact source content, ordinal, source reference and content hash |
| Assertion | Canonical subject/predicate/entity-or-literal fact with source evidence |
| Mutation | Durable admitted work and its state, separate from pipeline aggregate |
| Projection | Derived SQL/vector/graph artifact work with fenced claim and receipt |
| Evidence | Linked assertion/chunk/source span; not independently verified truth |

Catalog public IDs resolve inside the tenant. Physical storage keys are opaque;
passing a physical key as an external ID does not grant access. Agent and dataset
authorization are resolved from the session, never caller metadata.

## Admission and completion

`POST /v4/memory/insert` requires session, dataset, document, revision, chunk,
`title`, `source_ref` and exact `content`. See [API](docs/core/api-reference/) for bounds.
Admission returns `202` with candidate, mutation, pipeline-run and raw-log IDs.
This is durable admission, not visibility in every store.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> RECEIVED
    RECEIVED --> EXTRACTED
    EXTRACTED --> VALIDATED
    EXTRACTED --> REJECTED
    VALIDATED --> SQL_APPLIED
    SQL_APPLIED --> VECTOR_APPLIED
    VECTOR_APPLIED --> GRAPH_APPLIED
    GRAPH_APPLIED --> COMMITTED
```

The pipeline aggregate uses `QUEUED → RUNNING → EXTRACTED → VALIDATED →
PROJECTING → COMMITTED`. Technical recovery states include retry, dead-letter,
rollback and blocked cleanup. The SDK terminal set is `COMMITTED`, `REJECTED`,
`DEAD_LETTER`, `ROLLED_BACK`, `BLOCKED`; check status, not just method name.
Internal outbox/pipeline records may use `DLQ`; inspect each object's state.

Canonical `FactExtractionService` preserves zero-to-many extracted facts.
Validation mode 0 checks deterministically, mode 1 uses validator A, and mode 2
requires distinct A/B provider-model pairs. The runtime-selected policy is
snapshotted into admitted work; reserved `_mesa_*` metadata cannot downgrade it.
Rejected work may retain audit source but creates no active retrieval artifact.

Projection order is SQL → vector → graph. Separate stores do not share an ACID
transaction: fenced leases, receipts, ownership and reconciliation provide
idempotent convergence. A lost lease cannot finalize another owner's work.
Backpressure yields explicit admission errors; do not retry without bounds.

## Revision finalization and retries

For a multi-chunk revision set `finalize_revision=false` on all but the final
insert, with distinct chunk IDs and ordinals. The last insert freezes the
manifest. No new chunks may then enter that revision; the revision activates
only after every required child mutation succeeds. One document has one active
head. Create a new revision to change source content.

Use an insert `idempotency_key` (body field, <=128 characters) with the exact
same payload on retries. Conflicting payloads are rejected. Rebuild uses the
separate `Idempotency-Key` HTTP header. The SDK avoids unsafe automatic POST
retry after ambiguous failures; application recovery must inspect durable IDs.

`declared_content_hash` is the caller's whole-revision hash, `manifest_hash`
identifies frozen chunk membership, and a chunk `content_hash` identifies only
that chunk. Direct insertion does not establish a whole-revision hash.

## Correction, purge and rollback

Supersession retains historical assertions. A time-qualified query can include
eligible superseded evidence, which requires explicit producer validity dates (`valid_from` / `valid_to`); without them, superseded evidence is not returned. An unqualified query uses active evidence.
Rollback removes source ownership; shared artifacts remain while another active
source owns them. Tombstones precede secondary cleanup; failure stays `BLOCKED`.
Purge requires dataset `OWNER` plus explicit `PURGE`; replay/rollback require
the originating scope and explicit `ROLLBACK`. Semantic rejection cannot be
reopened through generic replay (`409 NON_REPLAYABLE`). Non-head historical
rollback is a conflict. Do not edit store rows or leases manually.

## Producer contract

Core consumes exact content and identity; [MESA_Data](docs/core/architecture/#ecosystem) owns source
acquisition, chunking and verified source metadata. HTTP insertion supports a
typed `legal_identity`; the current SDK `insert` signature does not expose it.
Use the HTTP contract for that field. Bare “MADDE 1” text is insufficient to
prove law identity. Producer metadata accuracy remains an external responsibility.

Canonical V4 insertion requires the combined processing consumer. A combined
runtime without models stores documents and finds them with BM25; vector search
starts when embedding is enabled (`degraded_sources` shows `vector` until then);
503 `canonical_processing_unavailable` happens only on a non-combined profile.

# Configuration reference

Source: `mesa_memory/config.py`, `load_runtime_profile` and `MesaConfig`.
Defaults below are field declarations, not evidence of an operational model.

## Startup and precedence

`MESA_RUNTIME_PROFILE` and `MESA_STORAGE_ROOT` are required by the runtime
loader. Profiles: `combined`, `test-isolated`. V4 requires one combined writer.
Storage aliases are tried in order ROOT, PATH, DIR, DB_PATH; a `.db` filename
selects its parent. Reject filesystem/home/repository root. Test-isolated
requires an absolute child of `MESA_RUNTIME_LAB_ROOT` and forbids models,
external providers and dotenv.

No implicit `.env` search. `MESA_LOAD_DOTENV=true` requires explicit
`MESA_DOTENV_PATH`; startup loads and reparses the explicit environment. The explicit dotenv file wins over existing environment values (`override=True`);
this can change profile/storage/provider flags, so review the file before enabling it. Pydantic constructor fields override
environment in direct programmatic configuration. Unaliased fields use their
uppercase field name; comments mentioning MESA_* do not create aliases.

`mesa start` and the Docker image provision an active local registry key and
credentials automatically; no bootstrap variables are needed in local mode.
`mesa start --host` controls the bind address (default `127.0.0.1`); the
credentials' client URL always uses `127.0.0.1`. The Docker image binds
`0.0.0.0` internally, while Compose publishes only to the host's loopback.
The direct runtime launcher requires `MESA_API_KEY` bootstrap or an existing active registry key at startup.
A bootstrap key requires the server-authored `MESA_PRINCIPAL_ID`; use offline
admin provisioning for ACL. `MESA_PORT` defaults to 8000; `MESA_LOG_LEVEL` to INFO
and `MESA_LOG_FORMAT` to json. Secrets must be injected privately.

## Providers and capacity

Model and external-provider flags default false. Validation defaults to
mode 0; mode 1 or 2 must be set explicitly via `MESA_TIER3_MODE`. Mode 2
needs distinct A/B validator identities. Extraction and validation are separate.
`MESA_EMBEDDING_ENABLED` and `MESA_EXTRACTION_ENABLED` each default to
`MESA_MODEL_ENABLED`. A combined runtime accepts writes with both off and finds
them through BM25. Disabled VECTOR lanes end `SKIPPED`; enabling embedding later
backfills them at startup using the same embedding identity. Backfill failures
leave committed records searchable.

`MESA_GRAPH_ENABLED` defaults to `true`, independently of the model flags.
Set it to `false` to avoid opening Kùzu in the runtime and offline rebuild
runner. GRAPH lanes end `SKIPPED`, BM25 and enabled vector search still work,
search reports `graph` in `degraded_sources`, and capability reports no graph.
Enabling it again backfills skipped GRAPH lanes at combined startup. A rebuild
with graph disabled also marks previously completed GRAPH lanes `SKIPPED` at
cutover so the new generation can be backfilled later. Existing graph files and
retained generations are not erased by changing this flag.

Local identity defaults to Magibu 768-d normalized; external text-embedding-3-small
requires setting dimension to 1536. Do not enable external flag and keep an
unrelated dimension. Nemotron-3 profile requires 2048 and `nemotron-qpass-v1`,
with query/passage input types. Provider/model/revision/dimension/normalization
define a fenced embedding space; switch through reindex/rebuild, not live fallback.

Install optional ML/provider SDK extras for the selected backend. With models
disabled semantic generation is intentionally unavailable. `MESA_ZERO_COST_MODE`
selects local Ollama configuration but preserves validator settings and does
not prove an air gap. RAM budget precedence is explicit MAX_RAM_MB/MAX_MEMORY_BYTES,
cgroups, psutil, then 1 GiB safe fallback; this is not an RSS guarantee.
Queue per-tenant bounds must fit within global bounds. `.env.example` deliberately
uses smaller sample global and per-tenant bounds than code defaults.

## Minimal V4 provider setup

Start with the disposable root, key and grants from the
[quickstart](docs/core/getting-started/#provision-before-startup), with the server stopped.
For an external OpenAI-compatible extraction + embedding setup, install
`uv sync --locked --python 3.11 --extra adapters` (no local ML extra is needed).
Select models supported by your endpoint. The following is an example pairing,
not evidence of a real-provider run:

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/mesa-doc-demos"
export MESA_STORAGE_ROOT="$(mktemp -d "$HOME/mesa-doc-demos/v4-XXXXXX")"
export MESA_PRINCIPAL_ID=docs-principal
export MESA_API_KEY="$(.venv/bin/mesa-v4-admin issue-key --principal docs-principal)"
.venv/bin/mesa-v4-admin grant-role --principal docs-principal --tenant docs-tenant --role OWNER
.venv/bin/mesa-v4-admin grant-agent --principal docs-principal --agent docs-agent --permission SESSION_CREATE
export MESA_RUNTIME_PROFILE=combined
export MESA_LOAD_DOTENV=false
export MESA_MODEL_ENABLED=true
export MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=true
export MESA_TIER3_MODE=0
export MESA_LLM_MODEL=openai:gpt-4o-mini
export MESA_LLM_API_KEY="${OPENAI_API_KEY:?Supply the provider key privately first}"
export MESA_EMBEDDING_MODEL=openai:text-embedding-3-small
export MESA_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
export MESA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY="$MESA_LLM_API_KEY"
export MESA_EMBEDDING_DIMENSION=1536
export MESA_EMBEDDING_NORMALIZED=true
export MESA_EMBEDDING_VERSION=v1
```

A root without active vector artifacts adopts a changed embedding identity at
startup and backfills skipped VECTOR lanes. A root with active vectors requires
an explicit rebuild before changing identity. Keep `MESA_API_KEY` (MESA access) separate
from `MESA_LLM_API_KEY` / `MESA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` (provider access). Modes 1/2 need
the validator A or A/B settings from the table below. Extraction is configured
separately and mode 0 still calls it.

`AdapterFactory` parses `provider:model` (`ollama`, `openai`, `openai_compatible`,
`anthropic`, `mock`). Embeddings support local sentence-transformers (`ml` extra) or
OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`adapters` extra); Claude/Ollama extraction does not
automatically configure embeddings. Native Ollama extraction requires a running
endpoint and an already available model; MESA does not provision it.

Select embeddings with `MESA_EMBEDDING_MODEL=provider:model`: `local:...`,
`ollama:qwen3-embedding:4b`, `openai:text-embedding-3-small`, or
`openai_compatible:nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b`. The second colon stays in the
model name. `MESA_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL` overrides the endpoint; Ollama otherwise
uses `<MESA_OLLAMA_URL>/v1` and needs no key for a local server.

### Local model servers and external providers (D31)

An endpoint is considered **local** when its scheme is `http` or `https` and its host is `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, or `host.docker.internal`.

- With `MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` (default):
  - `ollama` and `openai_compatible` (for both LLM extraction and embedding) are allowed on local endpoints (e.g. Ollama on `127.0.0.1:11434`, or vLLM on `127.0.0.1:8001/v1`; MESA itself uses port 8000) and forbidden on non-local/remote endpoints.
  - `openai_compatible` on a local endpoint requires no API key (the client sends `local` automatically).
  - External cloud providers (`openai`, `claude`, `anthropic`, `hosted`) remain strictly forbidden regardless of endpoint URL.
- With `MESA_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_ENABLED=true`:
  - Remote and cloud provider endpoints are allowed. Cloud providers and remote
    `openai_compatible` endpoints require configured API keys (`MESA_LLM_API_KEY`,
    `MESA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY`); local `openai_compatible` endpoints still default
    to `local`, and Ollama keeps its existing key-free behavior.

### Missing optional packages (P5-01)

If an optional provider or model extra is selected but not installed, server startup halts with a clear one-line installation command:
- Ollama LLM, Ollama embedding, or OpenAI-compatible embedding:
  `pip install "mesa-memory[adapters]"`
- Local transformer embedding (`sentence-transformers`):
  `pip install "mesa-memory[ml]"`

Endpoint/key settings retain the `MESA_LLM_BASE_URL` / `MESA_LLM_API_KEY` fallbacks for those providers.

With embedding enabled and `MESA_EMBEDDING_DIMENSION` unset, the server and
rebuild runner embed one probe at startup and use its length for storage and
admission. Probe failure stops startup and names the model and URL. Setting the
dimension explicitly skips the probe; embedding disabled with no dimension
keeps 768 and makes no embedding requests. The removed embedding provider,
external-model and local-model variables stop runtime startup with the
replacement setting. Nemotron still requires `MESA_EMBEDDING_VERSION=nemotron-qpass-v1`
and 2048 dimensions (explicit or detected).

The built-in `mock` adapter returns no extracted facts; it is not a source-backed
V4 demo. Contract tests inject deterministic fact and embedding providers
explicitly. Models-disabled startup, deterministic V4 tests and real-provider
V4 runs are different verification levels. V3 raw-memory processing requires
embeddings too; models-disabled boot does not demonstrate insert/search success.

## Environment file and first startup

The [template](https://github.com/Yasou13/MESA/blob/7062fafe2cff8442eb84d1da60df164099526c8e/.env.example) uses a standalone `combined` owner with models
disabled. Copy it only if needed, replace the storage path with an absolute,
writable dedicated directory, and supply issued credentials privately. To load
it explicitly, set `MESA_LOAD_DOTENV=true` and `MESA_DOTENV_PATH` to its absolute
path **in the launching shell**; setting them only inside the file cannot enable
loading. Do not load dotenv in `test-isolated`. The quickstart's exported settings
work without creating any `.env` file.

Fresh combined startup creates/migrates SQLite and initializes LanceDB/Kùzu;
there is no manual fresh-database migration step. Keep old storage migrations
separate: use the [upgrade procedure](docs/core/operations/#upgrade-v080), never delete an
existing database to resolve a startup error. Startup failures occur in the server terminal before
readiness; check the named variable, writable path or missing selected extra
there. Do not paste secrets or entire environment files into bug reports.

## Declared MesaConfig fields

Field-declaration reference; compare it with `MesaConfig` when configuration changes.
`required` or derived defaults are explicit. Legacy controls are present for V3;

| Python field | Environment name | Declared default |
|---|---|---|
| `llm_provider` | `LLM_PROVIDER` | `'claude'` |
| `llm_model` | `MESA_LLM_MODEL` | `''` |
| `llm_base_url` | `MESA_LLM_BASE_URL` | `None` |
| `llm_api_key` | `MESA_LLM_API_KEY` | `None` |
| `llm_timeout_seconds` | `MESA_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60.0` |
| `embedding_base_url` | `MESA_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL` | `None` |
| `embedding_api_key` | `MESA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` | `None` |
| `extraction_thinking` | `MESA_EXTRACTION_THINKING` | `False` |
| `extraction_max_tokens` | `MESA_EXTRACTION_MAX_TOKENS` | `4096` |
| `llm_embedding_model_name` | `LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | `'sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'` |
| `embedding_model` | `MESA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | `'local:magibu/embeddingmagibu-200m'` |
| `model_enabled` | `MESA_MODEL_ENABLED` | `False` |
| `tier3_mode` | `MESA_TIER3_MODE` | `None` |
| `tier3_llm_provider_a` | `MESA_TIER3_LLM_PROVIDER_A` | `None` |

# Retrieval, graph and evidence

## Four lanes and scoring

`MemoryDAO.search_v4_memory` is the canonical search primitive. Tenant, dataset,
agent, committed-state, jurisdiction and temporal eligibility are checked
before candidate rank contribution. Physical vector IDs and graph assertions
must agree with canonical ownership/evidence.

Scope predicates limit eligible rows; they are not evidence of statistically
independent rankings. The lexical query calls `bm25()` on the shared
`v4_assertions_fts` table. Do not infer complete cross-scope ranking isolation
from a WHERE filter or from the `scope_audit` label alone; candidate/rank and
observable diagnostic behavior require separate negative tests.

| Lane | Candidate signal |
|---|---|
| Vector | Compatible `ASSERTION_VECTOR` semantic representation; query embedding |
| BM25 | FTS5 passage/evidence and lexical matching; scoped typed citation lookup |
| Assertion | Predicate, subject, object/literal, evidence, token coverage and confidence |
| Graph | Bounded paths from legal, vector, lexical and entity-name seeds |

For candidate `c`, `RRF(c) = Σ w_lane / (k + rank_lane(c))`, with ranks starting
at 1, default `k=60`, and all four default weights `1.0`. Duplicate backend hits
cast one vote. Ties use candidate identity. The source is
`mesa_storage/retrieval_scope.py`; runtime overrides are in [configuration](docs/core/configuration/).

Lexical exact citation +200 and same-statute +40 change the BM25/lexical lane
ordering. Assertion exact citation +150 and same-statute +40 change assertion
ordering. These are **not RRF score increments**. After fusion a query-dependent
legal factor is applied: exact statute/article 1.5, same statute 1.25, competing
statute 0.25, otherwise 1.0. A query without recognized legal citations has
factor 1.0. HTTP/SDK `final_score` is final fused relevance; higher is better.
`rrf_score`, `legal_factor` and lane `raw_score` are separate diagnostics;
MCP response adapters may expose a normalized `score` field.

Typed ingestion identity uses a bounded alias ontology and immutable provenance.
It improves scoped pre-rank candidate discovery, including article chunks with
little title context. Reserved caller metadata cannot opt into trusted identity.
This contract checks structural linkage; it cannot prove a producer attached
the correct law, revision or real-world interpretation.

## Graph bounds and failure behavior

SQLite owns entities/assertions; Kùzu is a projection. Search uses at most 20
ranked seeds and 3 hops. The DAO asks for at most 500 graph hits; the provider
bounds frontiers to 64 and per-node fan-out to 32, with bounded native fetches.
The default graph request timeout is 15 seconds. These are traversal/resource
bounds, not exhaustive multi-hop completeness or latency guarantees.

Graph evidence preserves path assertion IDs, entities, predicates and direction,
and is reconciled against authorized canonical records. PageRank is telemetry
only. `graph_mode=disabled` turns off this lane for matched ablation; it does
not disable canonical assertion retrieval or graph projection writes.
Responses expose bounded `scope_audit`, `graph_ablation` and `vector_lane`
diagnostics. Their hashes identify contracts/config/scope, not a certification.

A configured operational backend failure yields explicit `503` rather than
silently claiming complete search. Projection-only graph adapters have no
neighbor implementation and report the capability false. A request timeout does
not permanently mark the graph provider unhealthy. Custom embedding providers
are configured but non-operational until a successful embedding call.

## Context and adaptive search

`GET /v4/sessions/{session_id}/context` defaults to `token_budget=2048` and
`retrieval_mode=single`. `ContextBuilder` packs evidence once using `cl100k_base`.
The budget applies to formatted model-visible context, not the entire HTTP
response. If canonical BPE cannot load, the current OpenAI counting path uses
one token per UTF-8 byte as a conservative offline upper bound, even when
`strict=True` is passed. This may pack less evidence and is not exact cl100k
measurement. Exceptions raised by the counting interface propagate.
Complete graph proof must fit atomically; compact proof retains canonical
supporting evidence and may omit optional structural details.

Adaptive mode plans only if Q0 is empty or no top-three candidate has two-lane
support. It sends only normalized query text to one planner call, accepts at
most two reformulations, rejects invented legal citations and reuses the original
scope. Outer query fusion uses Q0=1.0, Q1/Q2=0.5. `query_fusion_score` and
`query_origins` remain separate from lane provenance. Planner/expansion failure
preserves Q0. This mode does not generate an answer or certify model quality.

## Interpreting examples

For a neutral single-hop “archive hours” query, inspect source evidence and
mutation state. For a multi-hop query, require every supporting assertion in
the path; a reachable entity alone is insufficient. An empty result is a valid
no-evidence outcome, not proof that a statement is false. Version/date-sensitive
queries should supply timezone-qualified `valid_at` or an interval and, when
needed, jurisdiction. These are request patterns, not measured benchmark results.

Core context packing is distinct from the independently sealed Profile B
context and scorer in [E2E Certification](docs/core/architecture/#ecosystem).
